_comment: footer-leading-blank is off, on purpose. The parser reads any `token: value` line as the start of the footer block, so a body with a colon anywhere makes this rule inspect the line of prose above that colon and report a blank line that is not missing. Measured: it fires on a body reading `The split is deliberate: a README that grows to 800 lines stops being read` and on three of the five message shapes tried. Every commit in this repository has a prose body, so the warning was on nearly every commit, which trains people to ignore the tool.

What the rule would have caught is covered by the two things that own the trailer. .githooks/commit-msg writes it with `git interpret-trailers --in-place`, which writes the separating blank line itself, and scripts/test-session-guard.sh asserts the stamp is read back out of the trailers git leaves behind. Both are tests of the trailer; this rule was a proxy for it that also fired on prose.
Setting `parserOpts.footerPattern` does not help: the parser ignores it. Measured, not assumed. The remaining alternative is a custom rule, which is more machinery than the thing being replaced.
